rationale: The candidate reads as a compact split-wing mass with a legible dominant body and a central void, so it is coherent in multiple views rather than only one. The overall silhouette is not a staircase effect; it is a controlled interlock with one continuous rule. The main weakness is the access response: the verified frontage edge is not strongly converted into an obvious public seam or court, so the void feels internal rather than clearly street-serving. That said, the mass still plausibly supports neighborhood living: the three-part organization, modest upper variation, and carved center can accommodate active ground and shared space without collapsing into a sealed box. Repair integrity is strong because the form remains manifold-looking and visually continuous across views. References point toward a more explicit courtyard/threshold strategy and a clearer ground-level opening toward the public edge.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part composition with a central void and an upper connector can produce a clear public threshold while keeping the mass compact.
